positiveRealizations.interpretation: The week-26 construction pause removes the enterprise offer. Under the same keyed logit draw, buyer-10 chooses DIY instead of AI, and buyer-5 chooses the human instead of the enterprise. Subsequent provider beliefs, switching history and finite procurement choices diverge: buyer-10 generates five additional enterprise sales and buyer-5 two fewer, for net three. No initial quality failure is avoided in this case. The gain is a path-dependent pause/choice realization, not an executed improvement in unit delivery cost or quality.
positiveRealizations.causalLimit: This difference is caused by the modeled intervention, including its pause, conditional on the frozen simulator and seed. It is not an economically justified ex ante investment or evidence that this capability improves the production method. No pause-only ablation was registered or run; the explanation follows the archived sequence and unchanged effect parameters.

positiveRealizations.interpretation: The week-26 pause diverts buyer-1 to the human. In A, w26-buyer-1 is a rejected enterprise delivery; B therefore avoids that failed delivery and its adverse enterprise feedback. Later choices differ: B gains accepted enterprise jobs at weeks 34 and 36, and a rejected enterprise job at week 37. Total rejected jobs remain five in both arms; net accepted jobs increase by two. breakEven.classification: ANALYTICAL NECESSARY CONDITION; NOT A NEW MARKET SCENARIO OR OUTCOME RUN
breakEven.directRepaymentCondition: N * evidenced seller benefit per use >= complete oneoff cost + upkeep; foregone contribution, extra delivery costs and other burdens increase the requirement.
breakEven.zeroSupportedMarginalGain: At zero supported positive marginal delivery benefit, no finite positive-cost workload repays by the capability delivery-saving channel. Negative subcent CPU effects strengthen this conclusion. Incidental buyer-path gains in two saved realizations do not establish a repeatable productive benefit.
breakEven.workloadSource: Preselected reference/low/completed-research-replay/seed8001: 15 modeled second uses during weeks27-51, with no new demand after week51.

referenceCounterfactual.status: Reference cost is unaffordable in this seed at week26; 15 uses are borrowed only as a disclosed analytical workload from the funded low-profile replay. No reference investment is claimed.

assumedResidualLaborComparison.warning: Two minutes is an inherited unmeasured labor assumption, not a measured ceiling or demonstrated saving. The existing first asset already removed its separate assumed ten-minute finalization burden. The $0.25 tool cost is not assumed eliminated.

breakEven.missingObservation: Measure a repeatable incremental seller benefit against the strong incumbent on fresh independently accepted complete outcomes, measure complete construction/integration/upkeep tariffs, and show enough observed recurrence within the finite useful life. For the low illustrative 15-use case, even the optimistic necessary threshold requires more than $1.8313 per use before downtime; no such benefit was measured. For the reference threshold, eliminating the entire assumed two residual minutes would be insufficient.

costInterpretation.actualUnknownCase: All eight oneoff categories and maintenance are null. It blocks unconditional affordability and profitability; null is never zero.
costInterpretation.adaptiveVsResearchProvenance: Adaptive policy pays affordable search once and declines construction. Because the prototype was actually constructed during research, its remaining cost is disclosed outside enterprise cash and subtracted once for project-inclusive profit. This does not claim the adaptive enterprise constructed it or that research was operating-funded.
costInterpretation.completedReplay: If complete costs fit current generated resources, the replay debits them to the same ledger and simulates the constructed asset. With zero forecast productive benefit it is a funded but financially unqualified research attempt. Otherwise it stays unfunded, with outside research cost retained.
costInterpretation.seedVsSurplus: Seed cash, the $500 scenario commitment cap, future uncollected invoices, buyer savings, token value and enterprise valuation are not operating-generated funding. Historical opening research remains full-history cost; it is not debited again at the second checkpoint.

limits: Calibrated strategic simulation and conditional financial accounting, not actual market receipts or an equilibrium proof.
No price, demand, quality, human-effort, customer-effort or throughput improvement was assigned merely because the second capability exists.
B and C tie at the cent ledger; their signed measured CPU effects differ and are retained below one cent.
Nominal Monte Carlo mean intervals in the source are conditional on each scenario, unadjusted across the 80 groups, and do not quantify real-market demand or tariff uncertainty.
The two positive realized project differences are preserved; no post-outcome optimization or new pause-only trial was run.
